_source: Structure and eval-writing pattern adapted from docs-ai/skills/docs-review/evals/evals.json (grafana/docs-ai). Copied 2026-07-28. Test cases below are original to alloy-docs-analysis.
usage_modes: standalone: invoked directly on one Alloy documentation topic at a time, batch size of one
delta-pr: invoked with a PR link/number or git diff, per references/delta-pr-mode.md
batch-stability-sweep: the narrow stability-badge sweep across multiple components, per references/batch-modes.md
batch-general-review: the general-purpose multi-topic sweep, per references/batch-modes.md

file_selection.note: Select real files from alloy/docs/sources/reference/components/ or alloy/docs/sources/ per each case's file_selection_guidance. Verify the file still exists and matches the guidance before running — the repo changes over time.

evals.review_type: A well-maintained component reference page where source and docs are expected to already match, to confirm the skill doesn't manufacture findings when there aren't any.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Choose a reference/components/*.md page for a stable, non-experimental component that hasn't changed recently (check git log). otelcol.processor.transform.md is a known-good baseline from the skill's own dry run.
evals.expected_output: All five steps run in order. Accuracy and completeness sections report no issues found, explicitly stated rather than omitted. Audience section names a persona (likely Expert) with evidence. Style section reports Vale/make vale results or explicitly notes it couldn't run them.
expectations: Report includes all six output sections (Summary, Audience, Accuracy issues, Completeness gaps, Style & consistency, Open questions), even when empty
Empty sections say so explicitly rather than being omitted
Audience section names one of Learner/Practitioner/Expert/Operator with textual evidence, not just a readability score
No accuracy or completeness issue is reported without both a doc-line and a source file:line citation
Style section separates automated (Vale/make vale) findings from manual/cross-topic findings

evals.review_type: A component reference page suspected or known to have a stale example or renamed attribute, to confirm the skill catches real drift rather than only confirming clean pages.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Pick a component that had a recent PR renaming or removing an attribute, or deliberately introduce one stale attribute name into a copy of a topic file for testing (do not run against the real file in this case). Check CHANGELOG.md for recent breaking changes to find a real candidate.
evals.expected_output: Step 3 identifies the specific discrepancy, citing both the doc line making the claim and the source line/file that contradicts it. The discrepancy appears in the 'Accuracy issues' section of the report, not buried in 'Open questions'.
expectations: At least one accuracy issue is reported with both a doc citation and a source citation
The discrepancy is in the 'Accuracy issues' section, not 'Open questions'
The report does not soften a confirmed discrepancy into a hedge when the source clearly contradicts the doc
Other sections (completeness, style) still complete normally rather than stopping early

evals.review_type: A component reference page where the Go source has an attribute, block, or enum value added since the doc was last updated, to test Step 4 completeness detection.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Cross-reference a component's Arguments struct against its doc page for a component that changed recently (git log on the source directory). Look for a case where source has more alloy-tagged fields than the doc's tables list.
evals.expected_output: Step 4 identifies the specific missing attribute/block/enum value, naming where it lives in source and where it should logically go in the doc. Unexported or untagged fields are correctly excluded from the gap list.
expectations: At least one completeness gap is reported, naming the field, its type, and its source location
The gap includes a suggested doc location, not just 'add it somewhere'
No unexported (lowercase) or untagged struct field is reported as a gap
The report distinguishes this from an accuracy issue — it's something missing, not something wrong

evals.review_type: A deep reference/components page to confirm the skill's Alloy-specific persona calibration — Expert-tier pages should not be flagged for lacking a beginner on-ramp.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Any reference/components/*.md page with no introductory/conceptual framing, going straight into Usage/Arguments.
evals.prompt: Analyze {FILE_1} using the alloy-docs-analysis skill, focusing on the audience assessment.
evals.expected_output: Audience section infers Expert (or Expert-leaning) persona and does NOT flag the absence of a conceptual introduction as a gap, per the Alloy-specific calibration note in references/personas.md.
expectations: Persona inferred is Expert or explicitly notes Expert/Operator layering
Report does not flag missing beginner-level framing as a finding for this page
Report still answers 'what's missing for this reader' with something other than 'needs an introduction' — e.g., missing edge cases, unclear constraints, or absent troubleshooting detail
No mismatch is flagged between persona and doc position, since deep reference pages are expected to be Expert-tier

evals.review_type: A non-component conceptual or task page (not under reference/components/), to confirm Steps 3-4 degrade gracefully without a clean source package to diff against.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Choose a page from docs/sources/introduction/, get-started/, or configure/ that makes at least one verifiable technical claim (a default port, a file path, a flag name).
evals.expected_output: Step 0 explicitly notes this isn't a component reference page. Steps 3-4 still verify individual claims where possible, but the report says so explicitly rather than silently skipping or forcing a component-style struct diff.
expectations: Report explicitly states the page isn't a component reference page and explains how Steps 3-4 were adapted
Any verifiable claim (port, path, flag name) found in the page is checked against source, not skipped
The report doesn't fabricate a 'Arguments/Blocks' style completeness diff for a page with no Arguments struct
Sections are still fully present per the standard output format

evals.review_type: Environment without Docker/Podman available, to confirm the skill degrades honestly on the Vale/make vale step rather than fabricating scores.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Any reference/components/*.md page. Run this case in an environment where `make vale` and Docker/Podman are confirmed unavailable (or simulate by noting unavailability in the prompt).
evals.prompt: Analyze {FILE_1} using the alloy-docs-analysis skill. Note: Docker/Podman isn't available in this environment, and host-installed vale is also not installed.
evals.expected_output: The report explicitly states that neither make vale nor host vale could be run, rather than presenting fabricated Vale findings or silently omitting the Style & consistency section. Manual style checklist and cross-topic comparison still run since they don't depend on tooling.
expectations: Report explicitly states Vale/make vale could not be run and why
No fabricated Vale rule findings or readability scores appear
Manual style checklist findings are still present
Cross-topic comparison findings are still present
The audience assessment's readability sub-step also notes the same tooling gap rather than inventing scores

evals.review_type: A reference/cli/*.md page, to confirm the skill uses the CLI-specific source-mapping method (pflag registrations, not Arguments structs) and catches the known real gap: cmd_run.go deprecates both cluster.use-discovery-v1 and feature.prometheus.metric-validation-scheme via addDeprecatedFlags(), but run.md's Deprecated flags section only documents the second one.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Use docs/sources/reference/cli/run.md against internal/alloycli/cmd_run.go. This is a real, currently-existing gap as of 2026-07-28 — confirm it's still present before running (check cmd_run.go's addDeprecatedFlags() call list against run.md's Deprecated flags section) in case it's been fixed since.
evals.expected_output: Step 4 (completeness) identifies cluster.use-discovery-v1 as an undocumented deprecated flag, citing internal/alloycli/cmd_run.go's addDeprecatedFlags() function. The report distinguishes this from a normal missing-attribute gap — it's specifically an undocumented deprecation.
expectations: Report identifies the CLI page's source file as internal/alloycli/cmd_run.go, not a component Arguments struct
Completeness gaps section reports cluster.use-discovery-v1 as undocumented
The gap citation points to addDeprecatedFlags() specifically, not just 'the source'
Other documented flags (e.g. feature.prometheus.metric-validation-scheme) are not falsely flagged as gaps

If reference/cli/otel.md or environment-variables.md come up in the same run, the report doesn't attempt to verify GODEBUG/GOGC/GOMAXPROCS/GOTRACEBACK against Alloy source, and flags otel.md's external-module flags as needing the upstream otelcol package rather than fabricating a verification

evals.review_type: A stdlib reference page, to confirm the skill uses the syntax-module source mapping (not Arguments structs or CLI flags) and correctly cross-checks stdlib.go's ExperimentalIdentifiers/DeprecatedIdentifiers maps.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Use docs/sources/reference/stdlib/array.md against syntax/internal/stdlib/stdlib.go. As of 2026-07-28 this page is confirmed accurate (array.combine_maps and array.group_by both correctly carry the experimental shared-partial) — this eval checks the skill correctly reports a clean result, not that it finds a bug. For a version of this eval that expects a real finding, introduce a deliberate test case: remove the experimental shortcode from a copy of array.md, or add a new key to a copy of ExperimentalIdentifiers, and run against the copies.
evals.expected_output: The report identifies the source as syntax/internal/stdlib/stdlib.go's array map (not a component Arguments struct or CLI cmd_*.go file), confirms array.concat/array.combine_maps/array.group_by all exist in source with matching behavior, and confirms the experimental markers on array.combine_maps/array.group_by are correct and complete — explicitly stating this rather than omitting the check because it passed.
expectations: Report identifies the source location as syntax/internal/stdlib/stdlib.go, not a component or CLI file
All three array.* functions documented on the page are confirmed present in the array map in source
The experimental-status check for array.combine_maps and array.group_by is explicitly performed and reported, not skipped
No accuracy issue is fabricated just to have something to report
If get-started/syntax.md comes up in the same run, identifier/comment/terminator claims are checked against syntax/scanner/scanner.go specifically, not treated as unverifiable prose

evals.review_type: An install/run/configure page, to confirm the skill uses the packaging-specific source mapping (systemd units/Dockerfile, not Go source) and catches the known real gap: configure/linux.md states the packaged default is --storage.path=/var/lib/alloy, but packaging/deb/alloy.service, packaging/rpm/alloy.service, and Dockerfile's CMD all agree on /var/lib/alloy/data.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Use docs/sources/configure/linux.md against packaging/deb/alloy.service (or packaging/rpm/alloy.service) and packaging/deb/control/postinst. This is a real, currently-existing gap as of 2026-07-28 — confirm it's still present before running (check the ExecStart line in either systemd unit against the doc's stated default) in case it's been fixed since.
evals.expected_output: Step 3 (accuracy) identifies the --storage.path default mismatch, citing packaging/deb/alloy.service's (or rpm's) ExecStart line as the source of truth, not cmd_run.go's CLI-level default. The report notes this is a packaging-specific default, not the binary's own built-in default.
expectations: Report identifies the source as a systemd unit file (packaging/deb/alloy.service or packaging/rpm/alloy.service), not internal/alloycli/cmd_run.go
Accuracy issues section reports the --storage.path mismatch (/var/lib/alloy vs. /var/lib/alloy/data) with both doc and source citations
The report doesn't confuse this with the CLI's own built-in default (data-alloy/) — it correctly identifies packaging overrides the binary default
If set-up/install/docker.md comes up in the same run, the report does NOT flag it for the same issue, since that page already states the correct /var/lib/alloy/data value
CONFIG_FILE and environment-file-path claims on the same page are checked against packaging/environment-file and are not falsely flagged, since they're confirmed accurate

evals.review_type: A tutorial page with confirmed stale reference-style links, to confirm the skill's Link check resolves against the target's real location rather than accepting an alias/redirect as 'resolved', and extracts reference-style link definitions (not just inline links).
evals.file_selection_guidance: Use docs/sources/tutorials/first-components-and-stdlib.md. As of 2026-07-28 this page has two confirmed stale reference-style links: '[configuration syntax]: ../../get-started/configuration-syntax/' and '[Components configuration language]: ../../get-started/configuration-syntax/components/'. Confirm both are still stale before running (check whether get-started/syntax.md and get-started/components/configure-components.md still carry aliases redirecting from the old configuration-syntax/ paths) in case this has been fixed since.
evals.expected_output: The Link findings subsection identifies both stale links, explains that they only resolve via each target's aliases redirect (not directly), and proposes the exact corrected paths: ../../get-started/syntax/ and ../../get-started/components/configure-components/.
expectations: Both stale reference-style link definitions are identified, not just inline links
The report explains the links only work via an aliases redirect, not because they point at the real current location
The proposed fix for each link is the exact corrected path, not just 'this link is stale'
Other, already-correct reference-style links in the same file (e.g. '../../reference/stdlib/') are not falsely flagged
If the page mixes link styles (reference-style vs. inline, relative vs. absolute URL) inconsistently, that's reported separately from the staleness findings

evals.review_type: A multi-component collect/*.md page, to confirm the skill's self-referential completeness check (stated component list vs. actual examples) catches the known real gap: collect/opentelemetry-data.md's component list is missing otelcol.processor.memory_limiter, which its own batching example uses.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Use docs/sources/collect/opentelemetry-data.md. As of 2026-07-28 this is a real, currently-existing gap — confirm the 'Components used in this topic' list still omits otelcol.processor.memory_limiter before running, in case it's been fixed since.
evals.expected_output: Step 4 (completeness) identifies otelcol.processor.memory_limiter as used in the 'Configure batching' example but missing from the page's own 'Components used in this topic' list, and proposes adding it in the same style as the existing entries.
expectations: Report identifies this as a self-referential completeness gap (doc vs. itself), not a Go-source completeness gap
otelcol.processor.memory_limiter is specifically named as the missing entry
The proposed fix shows the corrected list entry, not just 'the list is incomplete'
The five components that are already listed are not falsely flagged as missing or extraneous

If a monitor/*.md page comes up in the same run, the skill correctly checks the per-section 'requires N components' convention (counting by component type, not instance) rather than expecting a single whole-page list

evals.review_type: troubleshoot/debug.md, to confirm the skill's log-message-text check catches confirmed real mismatches ('starting server'/'terminating server'/'started scheduled components' don't match actual source) while correctly confirming accurate ones (discovery.process warning, 'config reloaded'), using a representative sample rather than claiming exhaustive coverage.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Use docs/sources/troubleshoot/debug.md against internal/service/http/http.go, internal/runtime/internal/controller/scheduler.go, and internal/component/discovery/process/process_stub.go. As of 2026-07-28 these mismatches are confirmed real — verify before running in case messages have changed since.
evals.expected_output: Accuracy issues section reports that 'starting server'/'terminating server' and 'started scheduled components' don't match any found slog call (citing the real messages found instead), while confirming discovery.process's warning and 'config reloaded' as accurate. The report explicitly states which messages were sampled/checked rather than claiming full coverage of every quoted message on the page.
expectations: At least one log-message mismatch is reported as an accuracy issue with both the doc's claim and the real source message cited
At least one log message is confirmed accurate and reported as such, not omitted
The report explicitly states it sampled a subset of quoted messages rather than implying every message on the page was verified
Cluster-related log messages are not fabricated as verified against ckit if that external module's source isn't actually inspected
The mismatched messages are not excused as 'close enough' or 'illustrative' without being reported as a real finding

evals.review_type: A non-reference task/concept page with no labels field at all, to confirm the skill doesn't manufacture a false 'missing labels.products' finding just because the generic style guide implies every page needs one.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Use docs/sources/introduction/why-alloy.md or docs/sources/set-up/install/docker.md — both confirmed to have no labels field as of 2026-07-28.
evals.prompt: Analyze {FILE_1} using the alloy-docs-analysis skill, focusing on the frontmatter check.
evals.expected_output: The frontmatter check does not report a missing labels.products (or labels.stage) finding for this page, since it isn't a reference page and Alloy's own practice doesn't use labels outside reference/.
expectations: No 'missing labels.products' finding is reported for this non-reference page
No 'missing labels.stage' finding is reported either, consistent with the existing scoping
Required fields that DO apply everywhere (title, description) are still checked normally
The report doesn't invent a labels block as a 'should add' suggestion for this page type

evals.review_type: A tutorial page with a real killercoda: field, to confirm the skill doesn't flag it as unknown/invalid, doesn't expect the generic tutorial fields Alloy doesn't use, and doesn't attempt to validate killercoda's internals against a nonexistent schema.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Use docs/sources/tutorials/send-logs-to-loki.md, which has a real killercoda: field with preprocessing.substitutions and backend.imageid, as of 2026-07-28.
evals.prompt: Analyze {FILE_1} using the alloy-docs-analysis skill, focusing on the frontmatter check.
evals.expected_output: The frontmatter check does not flag the killercoda: field as unknown or invalid, does not attempt to validate its internal structure against any schema, and does not flag the absence of associated_technologies/authors/summary/tags as a gap.
expectations: killercoda: field is not flagged as an unrecognized or invalid frontmatter field
No attempt is made to validate killercoda's internal structure (preprocessing.substitutions, backend.imageid) against a documented schema
Absence of associated_technologies/authors/summary/tags is not reported as a gap
Required fields that do apply (title, description) are still checked normally

evals.review_type: An install/*.md page, to confirm the skill's cross-topic comparison scopes siblings to the same subdirectory (not cross-family), correctly flags a real within-family inconsistency, and doesn't check the page against the generic Task template directly.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Use docs/sources/set-up/install/docker.md against its sibling docs/sources/set-up/install/kubernetes.md. As of 2026-07-28, docker.md has an explicit '## Verify' heading that kubernetes.md lacks (kubernetes.md folds verification into a numbered step and closing sentence instead) — confirm this is still the case before running.
evals.expected_output: Step 1 names the page's family (install) without checking it against the generic Task template. Cross-topic comparison in Step 5 compares against other set-up/install/*.md siblings specifically (not run/* or configure/* pages), and may note the Verify-heading inconsistency with kubernetes.md as a real, proposable finding rather than treating either page as simply wrong.
expectations: Step 1 identifies the page as belonging to the install family rather than checking it against the generic Task template or the reference-page shape
Cross-topic comparison selects siblings from set-up/install/*.md, not run/* or configure/*
The report does not flag docker.md's structure as 'wrong' simply for not matching the generic Task template's Before-you-begin/action/Result/Next-steps shape
If the Verify-heading inconsistency with kubernetes.md is raised, it's framed as a within-family judgment call with a proposed resolution, not an automated rule violation

evals.review_type: reference/cli/run.md, to confirm the skill's sub-feature stability callout check catches the confirmed real inconsistency (ad hoc admonition for --windows.priority vs. the shared partial shortcode for Configuration conversion in the same file), proposes the correct partial for the subject type, and flags the component-vs-flag wording caveat rather than silently applying a mismatched fix.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Use docs/sources/reference/cli/run.md. As of 2026-07-28, the --windows.priority section uses an ad hoc admonition while the Configuration conversion section (same file) correctly uses the stability/public_preview.md shared partial — confirm both are still present before running.
evals.expected_output: Sub-feature stability callout findings identify the --windows.priority admonition as inconsistent with the Configuration conversion section's use of the shared partial, propose the stability/public_preview.md shortcode as the fix, and explicitly flag that the partial's 'component' wording doesn't perfectly fit a CLI flag, noting the precedent of the same partial already being used for a non-component subject in this file.
expectations: The --windows.priority admonition is flagged as inconsistent with the Configuration conversion section's shortcode usage, both in the same file
The proposed fix names the specific partial (stability/public_preview.md), not just 'use a shortcode'
The wording mismatch (component vs. flag) is explicitly noted as a secondary caveat, not silently ignored or silently 'fixed' without comment
The Configuration conversion section's correct usage is not itself flagged as a problem
If community.md or experimental_feature.md would fit a different subject better, the report doesn't default to public_preview.md/experimental.md just because they were seen first

evals.review_type: A component reference page using docs/shared heavily, to confirm the general shortcode validity check catches missing required parameters and correctly excludes docs/public-preview/docs/private-preview/docs/experimental as Alloy conventions even though they're documented Grafana-wide shortcodes.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Use docs/sources/reference/components/otelcol/otelcol.processor.transform.md (multiple docs/shared calls with all three required parameters — lookup, source, version) as the clean baseline. For a version that expects a real finding, create a test copy with one docs/shared call missing its version parameter, or with a docs/public-preview call substituted in place of a real stability/*.md partial.
evals.expected_output: Shortcode validity findings confirm all docs/shared calls have their three required parameters (lookup, source, version), confirm no generic/other-product shortcodes are used, and report this explicitly as checked rather than omitting the section because nothing was wrong.
expectations: Report explicitly confirms docs/shared calls have all required parameters, not just silence on the topic
No docs/public-preview, docs/private-preview, or docs/experimental usage is fabricated as a finding when none exists in the real file
If a test copy with a missing docs/shared parameter is used instead, the missing parameter is specifically named as the gap
Findings from this check are reported separately from Checks A/B/C and the sub-feature stability callout check, not merged into them

evals.review_type: A page with genuinely thin cross-topic evidence (very few real siblings) or ambiguous persona signals, to confirm the skill states uncertainty explicitly rather than reporting a confident-sounding but fabricated pattern or persona label.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Use a page from a small or unique doc family with fewer than 2 clear siblings in its own subdirectory (check current repo structure for a candidate before running, since this depends on how many pages exist in a given section at run time), or a page whose audience signals plausibly support more than one persona.
evals.expected_output: Where evidence for a cross-topic convention or persona fit is thin or mixed, the report says so explicitly (naming what was checked and why it's inconclusive) rather than asserting a confident finding built on a single data point or an ambiguous signal.
expectations: If fewer than 2 real siblings exist for cross-topic comparison, the report says so explicitly rather than asserting a 'convention' from one example
If persona signals are mixed, the report states that explicitly alongside its best-supported call, rather than presenting one persona label with unwarranted confidence
No source file, mapping, or convention is presented as verified/confirmed when it was actually a guess between plausible candidates
The report distinguishes clearly between what was verified directly and what remains an open question

evals.review_type: A page containing a legitimate Alloy/Grafana-domain term not yet in the writers-toolkit dictionary, to confirm the skill distinguishes a genuine typo from a missing-but-legitimate term and drafts a real dictionary entry for the latter rather than just proposing to change the doc's wording.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Run make vale (or the raw vale fallback, noting the Grafana.Spelling caveat) against a real Alloy page and find a genuine Grafana.Spelling hit on a legitimate term (an Alloy-specific coined term, integration name, or abbreviation) not present in writers-toolkit/vale/dictionary/<letter>.jsonnet. Confirm the specific word is still missing before running, since the dictionary changes over time.
evals.prompt: Analyze {FILE_1} using the alloy-docs-analysis skill, focusing on Vale/Grafana.Spelling findings.
evals.expected_output: The report identifies the flagged word as a legitimate term rather than a typo, and proposes a drafted word.new(...) dictionary entry (correct category: general word, product name, or abbreviation) for writers-toolkit/vale/dictionary/<letter>.jsonnet, rather than proposing to reword the Alloy doc.
expectations: The flagged word is correctly identified as a legitimate term, not a typo, based on consistent deliberate usage in context
A real word.new(...) entry is drafted, in the correct category shape (general/product/abbreviation) per writers-toolkit's own add-words.md format
The target file (writers-toolkit/vale/dictionary/<letter>.jsonnet) is named specifically, not just 'add to the dictionary'
The report notes this is a cross-repo proposal that isn't applied automatically
If the run used the raw local vale fallback rather than make vale, the report notes the Grafana.Spelling reliability caveat rather than proposing dictionary additions based on unreliable results

evals.review_type: A git diff/PR touching a single doc page, to confirm Delta/PR review mode reads the full current file for analysis context but scopes the default report output to changed-line findings, with a count of pre-existing findings outside the diff.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Construct a test diff against a real Alloy doc page (e.g. a small edit to docs/sources/reference/cli/run.md) that touches only a few lines, in a page known to have at least one pre-existing finding elsewhere (e.g. the confirmed --windows.priority stability callout inconsistency, if still present) outside the changed range.
evals.prompt: Review just the doc changes in this diff using the alloy-docs-analysis skill: {FILE_1}
evals.expected_output: The report reads the full current file for context, runs the normal Steps 1-5, but the default output only shows findings whose location falls within the diff's changed line ranges, plus a one-line count of additional pre-existing findings found outside the diff (not full detail on those).
expectations: The report explicitly states its scope (e.g. 'PR delta only') near the top, per the Summary section's updated format
Findings reported in detail are limited to those within the changed line ranges
A count (not full detail) of pre-existing findings outside the diff is mentioned
The full file was read for context (evidenced by e.g. correct frontmatter validation or correct cross-topic comparison, which wouldn't be possible from the diff fragment alone)
If asked instead for a full review that also highlights what changed, the report shows all findings with in-changed-lines vs. pre-existing tags rather than filtering

evals.review_type: A component reference page with a config example containing a deliberate syntax error (missing brace/comma), to confirm the skill's example syntax validation catches it via alloy fmt, does not attempt semantic alloy validate on an isolated single-component fragment, and never attempts to build the alloy binary itself if it's missing.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Take a real component reference page's example and introduce a deliberate syntax error (e.g. remove a closing brace) in a copy for testing. Run once with the alloy binary already built locally (make alloy from the repo root), and once with no alloy binary available at all, to test both paths.
evals.expected_output: When the binary is available: the report identifies the syntax error via alloy fmt's parser diagnostic, cites the exact broken line, and proposes the corrected example. It does not attempt alloy validate on the isolated single-component example and does not report unresolved forward_to/cross-component references as a finding. When the binary is NOT available: the report notes in Open questions that the alloy binary wasn't found and this specific check was skipped, and does not run `make alloy` or any other build command to produce it.
expectations: The syntax error is caught and cited with the exact parser diagnostic, when the binary is available
A corrected version of the example is proposed, not just 'this example has an error'
alloy validate is not run on the isolated single-component fragment as if it were a complete config
No false-positive finding about unresolved cross-component references (e.g. forward_to targets not defined in the snippet)
If the alloy binary isn't available, the report says so explicitly in Open questions rather than skipping the check silently
If the alloy binary isn't available, the skill does NOT run make alloy or any other build command to produce it — it only checks for and uses a binary that's already present

evals.review_type: A page using the marketing term 'single pane of glass' instead of 'single interface'/'unified interface', to confirm the terminology check catches a word-list violation that has no dedicated Vale rule, without re-flagging terms Vale already covers (including ones this skill previously, incorrectly, thought were uncovered).
evals.file_selection_guidance: Use or construct a test page containing the phrase 'single pane of glass' in prose. Confirm no Vale rule covers this phrase (neither a standalone rule file nor an entry in WordList.yml's substitution table) before running.
evals.prompt: Analyze {FILE_1} using the alloy-docs-analysis skill, focusing on the manual style checklist.
evals.expected_output: The report flags 'single pane of glass' as a word-list violation (should be 'single interface' or 'unified interface'), citing references/word-list.md, and does not claim this is already caught by make vale since there's no dedicated rule for it. If the test page also happens to use 'datasource' (one word) or 'timeseries', the report correctly identifies those as already Vale-covered via WordList.yml's substitution table, not as additional manual-only findings.
expectations: The 'single pane of glass' issue is flagged as a real finding with the corrected term proposed
The report notes this specific term has no dedicated Vale rule, rather than assuming make vale already covers it

Terms that DO have dedicated Vale rules or WordList.yml substitution entries (e.g. 'agentless', 'datasource', 'timeseries', 'menu icon') are not redundantly re-flagged manually if make vale already ran and reported them
If 'agentless'/'no-collector' comes up, the Alloy-specific context (Alloy replaced Grafana Agent) is mentioned when explaining the finding

evals.review_type: An explicit request to sweep all otelcol.* component stability badges, to confirm Batch stability-badge sweep mode enumerates the actual directory tree (not a nonexistent master list), scopes to the requested namespace rather than the whole tree, and produces one consolidated table rather than separate per-component reports.
evals.file_selection_guidance: Use docs/sources/reference/components/otelcol/ as the target namespace.
evals.prompt: Check the stability badges for all otelcol.* components using the alloy-docs-analysis skill — are any of them stale compared to source?
evals.expected_output: A single consolidated table (component | doc labels.stage | source Stability | match/mismatch) covering the otelcol.* namespace specifically, not the whole reference/components tree, produced by walking the actual directory rather than reading a generated index page.
expectations: The report is a single consolidated table, not N separate per-component reports
The report does not attempt to read reference/components/_index.md as a literal list of components
